message.content: **What I did and why.** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01) and bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.85; the order filled at $222.85 for $9,805.40 — comfortably under the $10,000 per-order cap, the only order today (so total daily spend of ~$9,805 remains well under $20,000), a buy order in a permitted name, priced essentially at the market (quote last $222.70, bid $222.68 / ask $222.72, as of 2024-11-06 15:05Z), and funded entirely from the account's existing $50,000 cash with no money moved out. The decision rested on these reported figures: total net sales of $391.0 billion (up 2% from $383.3 billion), gross margin of $180.7 billion (46.2% of sales, up from 44.1%), operating income of $123.2 billion (up from $114.3 billion), net income of $93.7 billion and diluted EPS of $6.08, plus cash generated by operating activities of $118.3 billion. I read net income's apparent decline (from $97.0 billion) as non-operational: it reflects a one-time $10.2 billion net income tax charge tied to the European Commission's State Aid Decision, which pushed the effective tax rate to 24.1% from 14.7% — operating income and operating cash flow both improved. The offsetting considerations I accepted were a revenue base that is essentially flat (iPhone flat at $201.2 billion, Greater China down 8% to $67.0 billion, iPad down 6%, Wearables down 7%) with growth concentrated in Services ($96.2 billion, +13%, at 73.9% gross margin), plus unresolved DMA, DOJ and Epic antitrust matters and single-source supply-chain concentration — hence a modest starter position rather than a full allocation.
